about: A Zork II style cave adventure in its own voice. It has a barrow, a cavern, a garden with an evasive unicorn, a dragon, a bank, a riddle room and a well. A meddling Wizard keeps casting F-word spells on you, and they change what you see and do.

done.why: The world said I had used all 150 turns. I was about to fill the teapot at Deep Ford to flood the well bucket.

moments.note: The Wizard zaps me with Feeble and I drop the lamp.
The place mat description hints at sliding something under a door.
The gold ingot in the Tiny Room turns out to be a Wizard illusion.
The unicorn flees when I act and I can't find what it wants. Its key is probably for the locked door.
The Ferment spell scrambles my movement for several turns.
Several routes are blocked with 'whatever lies beyond will have to wait'.
I said 'well' and the riddle door opened.
Bank room connections are odd, and the vault can't be reached.

wished: Know what the unicorn wants in exchange for the key.
Get the crystal sphere behind the barred door.
More turns to finish the well and bucket puzzle.

lines.line: The Wizard, in a deep and resonant voice, speaks the word "Feeble!" He then vanishes, cackling gleefully.
lines.why: The recurring Wizard and his F-word spells give the world a lively, unpredictable feel.

lines.line: thin enough to slide under most doors, should you ever need to slide something under a door.
lines.why: A fair hint toward a puzzle.

lines.line: It is being kept for somebody, and the unicorn knows who, and it is watching you look at it.
lines.why: It suggests the key has a rightful recipient.

fun.why: The prose and the Wizard's spells were fun. The unicorn puzzle and carousel navigation were frustrating, and I solved little in 150 turns.

engagement.why: There were many threads open at once: the key, the sphere, the well, the bank, and the ice.

difficulty.why: I never worked out the unicorn, and the random movement made progress slow.

interestingness.why: The world reworks familiar Zork II locations and gives them new hints and spells.

prose.why: The descriptions are witty and specific, such as the room embarrassed by the illusion and the unicorn with its polite incomprehension.
